correctness.rationale: Ren--Chen Theorem 1.2 establishes an exhaustive A/B/C-plus-40 family for omega=2; each family has N<2^(3e+2), e=v2(N). LTE for the four odd bases gives e<=5+log2(length), hence 3^(length-1)<2^17 length^3; the inequality fails from length=20 upward, yielding 3..19 and e<=9. Exact, standalone pure-Python trial-division construction enumerates every admissible family parameter, yielding 31 distinct integers, then exhaustively tests each of four bases and every possible length 3..19 using divisibility and exact digit quotient. Sole match 40=1111 base3, with sigma(40)=90=80+10 and 10 proper divisor. Both the finite bounds and every test step have been independently reconstructed; no extrapolation from a finite scan.

originality.rationale: The 2013 classification supplies parametrized families, but no repdigit intersection. The original 2022 preprint and 2023 published Theorem 1.3(a) instead assert that every repdigit in the stated range has fewer than three digits, and the base-3 table is empty; the exact base-3 tuple directly contradicts these assertions. The derived 2-adic bound and all-family finite sieve give a complete replacement for the natural odd-base, length-at-least-three regime. Targeted semantic and textual searches did not locate an equivalent correction. An independent priority review remains unperformed.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished later correction or independent exact odd-base classification could exist; negative search results alone are not a global priority proof.
The argument invokes the published Ren--Chen complete classification, examined but not independently re-proved here.

value.rationale: This naturally complete four-base classification resolves a direct contradiction in a 2022/2023 peer-reviewed repdigit theorem: base-3 emptiness and the two-digit bound fail at the exceptional near-perfect number 40. The 2-adic support-to-length reduction supplies a rigorous finite cutoff and a reproducible exact classification over all Type A/B/C forms rather than a cheap isolated numerical objection. It also complements the disjoint even-base analysis. No claim is made beyond the exact family.
